beats.text: You settled too early. Or you waited too long. Watch this.
Ten dates, one after another. Pass on someone, and they're gone.
The rule: just look at the first thirty-seven percent. Then take the first one who beats them all.
The rule finds the very best match forty percent of the time. Picking at random: about ten!

sources: Ferguson (1989), Who solved the secretary problem?, Statistical Science 4(3), 282–296 – optimal stopping: skip about n/e (≈37 %) candidates, then take the first one better than all before; finds the best with probability ≈ 1/e for large n.
Christian & Griffiths (2016), Algorithms to Live By – the 37 % rule applied to dating.
Simulation: 1,000 lives with 10 dates each, skip 3: the rule found the best one 401 times; taking the first date 90, a random pick 107.
